name: Irongate Security Vest
description:
A tactical vest in high-visibility yellow-green with SECURITY printed in large block letters across the back in retroreflective ink. Multiple exterior pockets with hook-and-loop and zipper closures — large enough for a baton, restraints, or a compact medkit. The front closes with a heavy-duty zipper and a snap-button placket. The back panel has a drag handle stitched into the collar. No armor, no electronics — just a well-organized piece of gear that announces your role and holds your equipment.

Irongate supplies roughly 40% of the private security firms operating in Tiers 2 and 3 of Meridian 88. This vest is so common it has become almost invisible — which creates its own particular problems for the people who depend on being recognized as security.
what_it_says: You're working a job that requires you to be seen. Whether that job is legitimate is a separate question.
worn_by: opportunists who bought one at surplus
story_hooks: Irongate vests are available at three different surplus markets on the Shelf — someone is stealing them in bulk and the company hasn't reported the thefts
A string of Tier 3 commercial burglaries all involved someone wearing an Irongate vest; no one questions security personnel
The drag handle on a particular vest has been reinforced beyond spec — someone modified it to serve a different purpose
